best_for: Windows developers who need a specific Community Edition build, for example to match an old project or keep a setup that predates the 2025.3 merge.
description:
IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition is the open-source build of JetBrains' Java and Kotlin IDE. Its code lives in the intellij-community repository on GitHub, which is also the open-source base of other JetBrains IDEs such as PyCharm. JetBrains says the IDE collects no usage statistics, logs or other data unless you agree.

If you move to the unified IntelliJ IDEA, you also get free Ktor framework support, Helm chart schema support, basic Thymeleaf highlighting, database connections with schema-aware SQL completion, and a Spring Boot project wizard. You can also build the IDE yourself: the repository explains how to clone it, fetch the Android modules and open it in IntelliJ IDEA.

points.title: Community is no longer a separate product
points.text: From 2025.3 JetBrains ships one IntelliJ IDEA installer, and the free core of that IDE replaces Community Edition. The unified IDE is the only edition that gets new features.

points.title: Updating from 2025.2 switches editions
points.text: Updating Community 2025.2 to 2025.3 turns the install into the unified IDE. You can also keep 2025.2 side by side while you move.

points.title: Pick 2025.2 or earlier for the classic build
points.text: If you want Community Edition as it was, choose 2025.2 or an earlier release from this list. Those builds no longer get updates.

points.title: Still free for work
points.text: Everything Community offered stays free in the unified IDE, for commercial and personal use, with no activation.

points.title: Open-source builds go to GitHub
points.text: The Apache-2.0 source stays on GitHub, with builds published there. They leave out AI Assistant, LSP support, Backup and Sync and Kotlin Notebook, though most can be added as Marketplace plugins.

points.title: Long history on Windows
points.text: This listing goes back to 2020.3 on Windows, for x64 and Arm64, with installers that run per user or for all users; releases winget lacks come from JetBrains' own release feed. There are no macOS or Linux entries for this edition here.
